item.content:encoded:

Sheriff's deputies responded to the scene and are working to determine what led to the incident. The investigation is ongoing, and authorities have not yet released additional information about the victim's identity or current status.

NewsRadio Pensacola will continue to follow this developing story and provide updates as more information becomes available from the Escambia County Sheriff's Office.

item.title: Pensacola Looks Beyond Bay Center With Broader Redevelopment Plan; Tech Park Investor Interested
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Pensacola officials are considering a broader redevelopment strategy for the area surrounding the Pensacola Bay Center — regardless of what ultimately happens to the arena itself. Councilwoman Allison Patton raised the idea during Monday's Community Redevelopment Agency meeting, calling for a more comprehensive…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Pensacola officials are considering a broader redevelopment strategy for the area surrounding the Pensacola Bay Center — regardless of what ultimately happens to the arena itself.


Councilwoman Allison Patton raised the idea during Monday's Community Redevelopment Agency meeting, calling for a more comprehensive look at the Bay Center area, Pensacola Technology Park, Wright and Alcaniz streets and connections between the district, downtown and Hollice T. Williams Park.


Rather than commission another isolated study, Patton said the goal would be to combine previous work into a broader plan addressing economic development, walkability, transportation and surrounding properties.


The discussion also produced a potentially significant update involving the long-vacant Technology Park.


Patton said there is an interested private investor discussing a partnership with the Pensacola-Escambia Development Commission on a speculative building at the site.

She said those discussions are underway and appear to be advancing. No potential investor was publicly identified during the meeting.


Mayor D.C. Reeves said the broader planning effort could examine streets, walkability, connectivity, the Tech Park and economic-development opportunities outside whatever footprint is ultimately used for the Bay Center.


The CRA generally supported continuing to develop the concept, although no specific planning contract or expenditure was approved Monday.

The idea comes as Pensacola and Escambia County continue discussing the long-term future of the Bay Center and surrounding publicly owned property.


The proposed CRA effort would focus on ensuring development around the arena site is coordinated with the larger downtown area rather than treating each property as an isolated project.

item.title: Florida Medicaid Fraud Crackdown Saves Nearly $1 Billion in ABA Spending
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis announced results Tuesday from Florida's enhanced Medicaid integrity initiative, which has already identified widespread fraud and abuse across the state's health care programs. The effort, launched in June as what state officials describe as the most significant Medicaid integrity initiative in Florida history, has shifted…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis announced results Tuesday from Florida's enhanced Medicaid integrity initiative, which has already identified widespread fraud and abuse across the state's health care programs. The effort, launched in June as what state officials describe as the most significant Medicaid integrity initiative in Florida history, has shifted away from a traditional "pay-and-chase" model toward preventing fraud before taxpayer dollars are spent.

The numbers are substantial. Since January, the Agency for Health Care Administration has conducted more than 400 provider site visits, placed more than 260 providers on payment restrictions or suspended them entirely, and terminated more than 220 providers from Florida Medicaid for fraud, waste, or abuse. Those terminated providers had billed Medicaid for more than $230 million in 2025. Additionally, AHCA has referred more than 150 cases to the Attorney General's Office based on fraud allegations.

The most dramatic savings have come from Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) services, where enhanced oversight and managed care transitions have reduced projected annual spending from $3.86 billion to $2.88 billion—a nearly $1 billion reduction. AHCA investigators uncovered troubling billing practices, including providers billing Medicaid for more than 24 hours of services in a single day and charging for consecutive days of service spanning weekends and holidays. The state also created an ABA Task Force to strengthen accountability within that sector.

AHCA Secretary Shevaun L. Harris said the effort targets "bad actors who exploit the Medicaid program, not legitimate providers delivering necessary care to Floridians," emphasizing that the initiative protects children, pregnant women, seniors, and disabled residents who depend on the program.

item.title: Pensacola CRA Advances $695,000 Bayou District Contract for Former Baptist Hospital Campus
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- A controversial consulting firm could return to work on redevelopment of Pensacola's former Baptist Hospital campus after receiving a recommendation from the city's Community Redevelopment Agency. The CRA voted 5-1 Monday to recommend a $695,000 development-advisory contract with Bayou District Consulting. The…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- A controversial consulting firm could return to work on redevelopment of Pensacola's former Baptist Hospital campus after receiving a recommendation from the city's Community Redevelopment Agency.


The CRA voted 5-1 Monday to recommend a $695,000 development-advisory contract with Bayou District Consulting.


The company was at the center of significant public opposition during an earlier redevelopment proposal for the property.


That opposition resurfaced Monday. Residents Harper Cummings and Girasol Alfonso urged the CRA to reject Bayou District, raising concerns about the company's previous work and its earlier involvement in discussions surrounding the Baptist property.


CRA Chairman Delarian Wiggins defended the latest selection process and encouraged Bayou District representatives to directly involve opponents in future community discussions.

City officials also stressed that the new proposal is different from the one considered previously.


Councilwoman Jennifer Brahier said the earlier process left open the possibility that the consultant could eventually become the project's developer.

The new contract, she said, is strictly for consulting.


Bayou District principal Jerry Beruse told the CRA that the firm's job would be to meet with residents, city officials and other stakeholders and determine what redevelopment concepts are feasible for the property.


Any eventual selection of a developer would come through a separate process.

Before considering the contract, the CRA unanimously recommended shifting $395,000 from a Westside façade-improvement program to complete funding for the consulting work.


The Bayou District contract still requires City Council approval.

item.title: Trump Dyed-Diesel Order Delivers Federal Relief Northwest Florida Farmers Sought
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Santa Rosa County, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- A fuel-cost break Northwest Florida farmers told NewsRadio they were seeking last week is now moving forward at the federal level. President Donald Trump signed an executive order Monday temporarily easing federal restrictions on red-dyed diesel, fuel normally reserved for off-road equipment such as…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- A fuel-cost break Northwest Florida farmers told NewsRadio they were seeking last week is now moving forward at the federal level.


President Donald Trump signed an executive order Monday temporarily easing federal restrictions on red-dyed diesel, fuel normally reserved for off-road equipment such as tractors and other agricultural machinery.


The order directs the federal government not to impose the normal penalty for highway use of dyed diesel from Oct. 5 through Dec. 31. It also directs Treasury to determine whether certain federal excise-tax payments can be deferred and potentially further relieved.


The issue has direct implications for Northwest Florida agriculture.

Santa Rosa County Farm Bureau President Ryan Jenkins told NewsRadio 92.3 last week that farmers had been seeking temporary relief during harvest season.


Farmers can already use dyed diesel in off-road equipment without paying highway taxes. The problem comes when fuel is needed for trucks and other vehicles operating on public roads during harvest.


Jenkins said the final months of the year account for a significant portion of many farms' annual fuel consumption. He noted that a large tractor can burn around 200 gallons in a day, while a cotton picker can consume roughly 350 gallons.


The White House says the federal diesel excise tax is 24.4 cents per gallon. The administration is also encouraging states to take corresponding action on their own taxes and restrictions.


That makes Florida's response the next issue to watch for Northwest Florida farmers.

item.title: Pensacola CRA redirects $395K from facade grant to Baptist Hospital Legacy Campus project

The move represents a shift in how the agency is deploying available funds to accelerate work on the legacy…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Community Redevelopment Agency has reallocated $395,000 from an underutilized facade improvement grant program to help fund redevelopment efforts at the Baptist Hospital Legacy Campus, according to a Citizen Portal report.

The move represents a shift in how the agency is deploying available funds to accelerate work on the legacy hospital property, a site that has drawn significant interest for mixed-use redevelopment in downtown Pensacola. The facade grant program, which had not been fully tapped, was identified as a source for redeployment.

Details on the specific timeline, scope of work, and partnership structure for the Baptist Hospital Legacy Campus project were not immediately available. The redevelopment has been a focal point for economic development discussions in Escambia County.

item.title: Sheriff Simmons: Escambia Deputy Recruiting Has Rebounded After Years of Vacancies
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- The Escambia County Sheriff's Office says it has largely overcome a recruiting problem that once left dozens of deputy positions vacant. Sheriff Chip Simmons told NewsRadio 92.3 Tuesday morning that the agency previously carried between 30 and 40 vacancies at a time. That made adding additional positions difficult…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- The Escambia County Sheriff's Office says it has largely overcome a recruiting problem that once left dozens of deputy positions vacant. Sheriff Chip Simmons told NewsRadio 92.3 Tuesday morning that the agency previously carried between 30 and 40 vacancies at a time.


That made adding additional positions difficult to justify, Simmons said, because the Sheriff's Office was already struggling to fill the jobs it had.

That situation has changed considerably.


Simmons said the agency now averages fewer than 10 vacancies and can generally hire enough qualified applicants to fill its available positions.

The Sheriff's Office also recently added eight deputy positions as part of a three-year staffing agreement with Escambia County.


That agreement calls for eight additional deputies per year over three years, for a total of 24. Simmons says the additional positions were intended to move Escambia closer to the statewide staffing benchmark for deputies per population.

Twelve recruits are currently going through the agency's law-enforcement certification program.


Simmons said improved recruiting is also allowing the agency to begin thinking more about succession planning — including preparing replacements for deputies expected to retire or leave.


The sheriff said the agency can temporarily “overfill” positions in anticipation of departures, although there is currently no dedicated budget for doing so.

item.title: Invest 92L: Escambia Steps Up Preparations as Gulf System Threatens Heavy Rain
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Escambia County is stepping up preparations as Invest 92L becomes increasingly likely to develop into a tropical depression in the Gulf. The National Hurricane Center raised development chances to 90% Tuesday morning and said a tropical depression is anticipated within the next day or so. The system is expected to…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Escambia County is stepping up preparations as Invest 92L becomes increasingly likely to develop into a tropical depression in the Gulf.


The National Hurricane Center raised development chances to 90% Tuesday morning and said a tropical depression is anticipated within the next day or so. The system is expected to move generally east before eventually turning north or northeast toward the northern Gulf Coast.


While the eventual track and intensity remain uncertain, Northwest Florida is now among the areas being told to closely monitor the system.

Escambia County Emergency Management says it is monitoring conditions around the clock. County crews are also watching problem creeks and rivers, and free sand has been made available to residents at several locations.


Beach conditions are already becoming hazardous. Escambia County says all county beaches face a high risk of life-threatening rip currents through Saturday, with high surf and heavy rainfall among the other potential impacts.


Pensacola Yacht Club is also preparing. Commodore Steve Cozart told members Tuesday that a decision on whether to evacuate the marina will be made by Wednesday evening. Boat owners are being encouraged to remove canvas, secure sails and make sure boats in dry storage are properly secured.


NOAA aircraft are expected to gather additional atmospheric data around the disturbance Tuesday, with Air Force reconnaissance scheduled for Wednesday.

The National Hurricane Center's next scheduled Tropical Weather Outlook is expected Tuesday afternoon.


NewsRadio 92.3 will continue monitoring the system and local preparations as the forecast becomes clearer.

item.title: Culinary Productions opens new intimate event venue in downtown Pensacola
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Culinary Productions has announced the opening of Our Garden, a new event venue at 811 W. Garden Street designed for smaller celebrations of up to 75 guests. The space will begin hosting events in December and is already accepting reservations. The venue will accommodate weddings, micro weddings, bridal and baby showers, corporate holiday parties,…
item.content:encoded:
Culinary Productions has announced the opening of Our Garden, a new event venue at 811 W. Garden Street designed for smaller celebrations of up to 75 guests. The space will begin hosting events in December and is already accepting reservations.

The venue will accommodate weddings, micro weddings, bridal and baby showers, corporate holiday parties, rehearsal dinners, and other private events. It features an outdoor garden courtyard for ceremonies and gatherings, with catering provided by Culinary Productions.

"For more than 20 years, we've had the privilege of being part of some of the most important celebrations in our clients' lives," said Mike DeSorbo, owner of Culinary Productions. "Our Garden gives us an opportunity to offer something different — a warm, intimate setting created specifically for smaller gatherings."

Culinary Productions, which has been operating as a full-service catering company since 2004, now expands its event services to include this dedicated venue space. Interested clients can visit culinaryproductions.net to schedule a tour or make a reservation.

item.title: Santa Rosa County offers low-cost pet vaccination clinic October 24
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County Animal Services is hosting a drive-through vaccination and microchipping clinic Saturday, October 24, from 10 a.m. to noon at 4451 Pine Forest Road in Milton. The clinic will serve cats and dogs with rabies vaccinations, microchips, and additional vaccines to prevent common illnesses like parvovirus and panleukopenia. Services…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County Animal Services is hosting a drive-through vaccination and microchipping clinic Saturday, October 24, from 10 a.m. to noon at 4451 Pine Forest Road in Milton. The clinic will serve cats and dogs with rabies vaccinations, microchips, and additional vaccines to prevent common illnesses like parvovirus and panleukopenia.

Services are priced at $15 for microchipping, $10 for rabies vaccination, $10 for additional vaccines, and $10 for bordetella, with a total of $45 for all services. Pet owners can register individual animals online and pay in advance — only those services selected will be charged. All pets must be registered and prepaid by Tuesday, October 20, or they won't be admitted to the clinic. Those without internet access can register in person at the shelter during regular business hours.

Participants must be Santa Rosa County residents with a valid ID. Cats must arrive in a carrier, and dogs must be leashed with a collar. County Animal Services asks that community members arrive early and expect longer waits, since microchip insertion and scanning takes extra time. Traffic will be heavy, so the county recommends entering Pine Forest Road from the north (Old Bagdad Highway) and exiting from the south (Carroll Road). For more information or to register, call 850-983-4680.

item.title: West Pensacola Elementary, Running Wild Launch Socktober Drive for Veterans, Homeless
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: West Pensacola Elementary School and Running Wild are teaming up for the sixth annual Socktober donation drive, running through October 31 to collect socks and essential items for people in need across Pensacola. The campaign aims to collect 3,500 pairs of new socks this year—up from 2,923 collected last year since the drive launched in 2020 with…
item.content:encoded:
West Pensacola Elementary School and Running Wild are teaming up for the sixth annual Socktober donation drive, running through October 31 to collect socks and essential items for people in need across Pensacola.

The campaign aims to collect 3,500 pairs of new socks this year—up from 2,923 collected last year since the drive launched in 2020 with just 422 pairs. For the first time, donated socks will be distributed not only to individuals experiencing homelessness through Opening Doors Northwest Florida but also to local veterans via the VA clinic, expanding the program's impact.

Donation drop-off locations include Running Wild at 3012 E. Cervantes Street and 72A South Section Street in Fairhope, West Pensacola Elementary at 801 N. 49th Avenue, and select local businesses. Beyond socks, the community can donate jackets, blankets, shoes, hats, rain gear, bottled water, and other essentials. According to organizers, socks are among the most-needed yet overlooked items for people without stable housing, offering warmth and dignity as weather cools.
